item.title: New Manager, Same Problems, Liverpool Thrash 10-Man Man Utd In Pochettino’s First Match
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. Manchester United’s Argentinian head coach Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Liverpool’s Spanish midfielder #23 Victor Munoz (L) celebrates with Liverpool’s Dutch defender #30 Jeremie Frimpong (R) after scoring their fourth goal during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. item.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
item.description: …Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats …FG backs probe of incident …Diri makes case for senatorial roads By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with more than 51 survivors recorded, as search and recovery operations continue. President Bola Tinubu has also approved N250 million to support families of the victims and directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities. Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to Bayelsa State on the President’s directive. The boat, which was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony, capsized near Oweikorogha community, leaving several persons dead and others rescued. Speaking at the Government House, Yenagoa, after visiting hospitalised survivors at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital (BMUTH), Shettima said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to collaborate with the state government in the search and rescue operations and provide support for those affected. He described the incident as a national tragedy, noting that behind the casualty figures were individuals with families, relationships and responsibilities to their communities and society. “Each person involved has a name, an identity, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Family members cannot come to terms with the fact that someone who left home for a funeral will never return,” he said. The Vice President acknowledged the peculiar geographical challenges of Bayelsa, where waterways serve as major transportation routes connecting communities to schools, hospitals, markets and other essential services. “Geography can determine how people travel, but it will never determine the worth of the lives involved,” Shettima stated. He disclosed that Tinubu had directed the NDDC to procure boats to improve transportation in the riverine areas of the state. Shettima also commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the tragedy and the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the incident. He stressed the need for the recommendations of the panel to be implemented to prevent a recurrence. In his remarks, Diri thanked Tinubu and the Vice President for their intervention and for identifying with the people of Bayelsa at a difficult time. The governor recalled that Shettima was among the first senior government officials to contact him following the incident, alongside the President’s Chief of Staff and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures. ‎ ‎”We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence. ‎ ‎”President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. item.title: Hypo Partners With NCDC In Support Of Efforts Against Ebola Virus Disease
item.description: Hypo Homecare Products Limited, makers of Hypo household hygiene products, has extended significant product support to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention in support of national efforts to strengthen preparedness and response against Ebola Virus Disease in Nigeria. The contribution of Hypo Bleach is aimed at supporting critical infection prevention and control efforts, particularly within healthcare facilities, and reinforcing the collective effort to safeguard public health and protect communities across the country. The donation, which was formally presented to the NCDC, was received on behalf of the Centre by Tajudeen Arowolo, Head of Department, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response. The gesture reflects Hypo’s commitment to supporting public health efforts and promoting better hygiene and sanitation practices across Nigerian communities. The NCDC welcomed the contribution as Hypo reaffirmed its commitment to playing a role in the collective effort to protect public health. As a household hygiene brand with a longstanding commitment to keeping homes and shared spaces clean and hygienic, Hypo recognises the importance of proper hygiene and environmental sanitation in supporting public health. Through its range of cleaning and disinfection products, the brand continues to encourage consumers to maintain cleaner and more hygienic environments. Speaking on the donation, Ifeoluwa Adeyemo, Senior Brand Manager, Hypo , said: “At Hypo, we believe that protecting public health is a collective responsibility. As a brand committed to providing effective cleaning and disinfection solutions, we recognise the importance of supporting efforts that promote healthier and safer communities. This donation is our way of contributing to the ongoing efforts against Ebola Virus Disease and demonstrating our commitment to the well-being of Nigerians.” Acknowledging the contribution, Dr. Odianosen Ehiakhamen, Incident Manager for Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria , said: “We’re grateful for the support we have just received from Hypo, providing us with IPC commodities to strengthen IPC practices, especially in health facilities. These cartons of hypochlorite solution will go a long way in supporting health facilities in the states, particularly through the state preparedness and response systems for Ebola Virus Disease and other outbreak diseases. Thank you so much, Hypo, for the support.” Beyond the product donation, Hypo is also committed to supporting broader public awareness efforts through hygiene education. The brand recognises that access to effective hygiene solutions must go hand in hand with the knowledge and adoption of appropriate hygiene practices. Through planned public awareness and hygiene education initiatives, Hypo aims to encourage better hygiene habits, promote responsible sanitation practices and reinforce the importance of maintaining clean and hygienic environments in homes and communities. item.title: Iran unveils new missile launcher as commanders issue warning to US
item.description: Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic’s capabilities in defiant messages to the United States. “A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time,” Iranian state television reported on Saturday. State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards’ aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base. The two commanders were shown riding atop a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment. “The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation,” said Vahidi, whose Revolutionary Guards form the ideological arm of Iran’s military. “Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy,” said Mousavi. The unveiling comes months into the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the conflict. During the war’s most intense phase, US-Israeli strikes targeted Iran’s missile capabilities and again hit its nuclear sites, though the extent of the damage remains unclear. Earlier this month, Iran unveiled a new underground missile base housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers. item.title: Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31
item.description: The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey. The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at COP31, expressed deep dismay as the talks broke down. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. – ‘Greenwash’ – Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory” as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. – Falling short – The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy. “It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited”. “The world cannot afford a repeat.” Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process. item.title: Tinubu Is A Covenant Child, Any Conspiracy Against Him Shall Be Consumed By Fire — Akpabio
item.description: Senate President Godswill Akpabio has said that plans by the opposition to conspire against President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election in the 2027 general elections, will not stand. Akpabio, who spoke at the PBAT Door-To-Door campaign in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Sunday, described Tinubu as a child of covenant, saying any conspiracy against him “shall be consumed by fire.” He said that the National Assembly is behind the President 100 per cent. The senator listed key achievements of the Tinubu administration, including infrastructure, NELFUND for students and other empowerment programmes. According to him, those who want to reverse the fuel subsidy removal are confused. The former Akwa Ibom governor also said that all political parties in the state have collapsed into one to support Tinubu’s re-election. Akpabio noted that the opposition does not have a footing in the state. He commended the PBAT Door-To-Door movement for recognising the importance of Akwa Ibom voters by bringing their campaign to their doorsteps. item.title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him. The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation. The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets. He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced. “Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said. Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways. He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation. The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims. He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence. item.title: Otti begins construction of new Umuahia traffic corridor
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas. The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capital Development Authority (UCDA), is designed to provide an alternative traffic corridor, ease congestion around Government House and Isigate, and improve connectivity within the state capital. The General Manager of UCDA, Engr. Kingsley Agomoh, who conducted journalists round the project site, said the road would allow motorists coming from Bende and Ikot Ekpene roads to connect to Abia Line, Aguiyi Ironsi Boulevard, Abia Express Tower and Onuimo Road without passing through the Government House axis. He said the project would significantly reduce traffic pressure on major roads, stimulate economic activities and improve the aesthetics of Umuahia. ” If you are coming from Bende Road, you pass through the Post Office Tower, cross the railway station and connect to First Bank, Ridge Club and Abia Line without going through the Government House axis,” Agomoh said. He explained that the project was part of Otti’s broader urban renewal programme, adding that the governor had also directed the relocation of Umuahia Railway Station to the Nnennaya Oti Bus Terminal. According to him, the state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Railway Corporation to facilitate the construction of the access road across the railway corridor. Agomoh also disclosed that another road linking First Bank to the Keystone, Sterling and FCMB bank areas would be reopened and reconstructed to provide motorists, particularly those coming from the Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia, with a shorter alternative route. He said the road, which had been encroached upon by adjoining property owners, was being reclaimed to restore access and ease movement within the commercial district. Describing the railway-crossing road as a signature project of the Otti administration, Agomoh said the governor’s urban renewal drive was repositioning Umuahia for increased economic activities and orderly development. He urged Abians to support Otti and other Labour Party candidates in the 2027 elections, arguing that continuity would ensure the completion of ongoing infrastructure projects across the state. item.title: Alia, Akume, Suswam, others meet over Benue APC crisis
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue State has reiterated his commitment to reconciliation and unity within the All Progressives Congress (APC) following a meeting with prominent party stakeholders in Abuja. The meeting, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, was convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by former Katsina State Governor, Senator Ibrahim Shema, as part of efforts to resolve disagreements among party leaders in Benue. Those in attendance included the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume; former Benue State Governor, Senator Gabriel Suswam; Senator Barnabas Gemade; Senator Jack Gyado; and Elder Simon Shango. Alia disclosed the meeting in a post on his verified social media handle, saying the engagement lasted about two hours and provided an opportunity for the stakeholders to discuss the future of the party in the state. He said: “Today, (Saturday, November 21, 2026) I joined fellow Benue APC stakeholders in Abuja for a reconciliation meeting convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by Sen. Ibrahim Shehu Shema, former Governor of Katsina State. “The meeting, which lasted about two hours, brought together the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Sen. George Akume, former Benue State Governor, Sen. Gabriel Suswam, Sen. Barnabas Gemade, Sen. Jack Gyado and Elder Simon Shango. “I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain. “My commitment is clear. I will continue to engage with our leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while keeping the peace, security and development of Benue State at the centre of my work. “The people of Benue entrusted us with the responsibility to serve, and that responsibility must continue to guide us.” The post Alia, Akume, Suswam, others meet over Benue APC crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
item.description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja. The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children. Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together. He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter. “Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said. He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court. The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano. “Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said. Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details. Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react. “I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked. He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him. The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15. The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings. The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress. item.title: Photos: Gunmen set Plateau secondary school ablaze in Bokkos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, triggered panic in the community after residents noticed smoke billowing from the school premises shortly after church service. A community member, Daniel Bwehfa Makodeng, who reported the incident to journalists, said the school was set ablaze at about 1pm. “Suspected bandits set the school on fire around 1pm,” he said. He explained that residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering about 30 minutes later that the building was on fire. The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Hon. Amalau Amalau, also confirmed the incident, saying the council had received reports that the school was engulfed in flames. Speaking in a telephone interview, Amalau said the circumstances surrounding the fire and the identities of those responsible had yet to be established. “We only saw the school in flames. We cannot ascertain at the moment who was responsible or whether it was carried out by terrorists,” he said. The chairman confirmed that the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the immediate concern was the destruction of the school building. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, extend La Liga lead
item.description: Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. “We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.” The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide. The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up. – Quickfire treble – Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute. Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated. “The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN. Later Sunday Atletico Madrid, third, visit Getafe among other fixtures. Vanguard News The post Barcelona

item.title: Katsina ADC Gov Candidate Kaita Launches 2027 Campaign
item.description: The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Katsina State, Senator Ahmed Kaita, has officially launched his 2027 campaign in the Funtua senatorial zone, drawing a crowd of supporters as residents of Funtua Local Government pledged to back ADC candidates in all elective positions during the forthcoming general elections. The campaign rally, held on Sunday at Aya Primary School in Funtua, attracted scores of supporters from across Funtua and neighbouring communities, signalling the party’s determination to mount a strong challenge in the state. Addressing the crowd, Senator Kaita expressed gratitude for what he described as the overwhelming voluntary turnout of supporters, insisting that those in attendance were driven by a genuine desire for change and good governance rather than political inducement. The event attracted scores of supporters from across Funtua and neighbouring communities. He said the campaign would unveil its comprehensive policy agenda during the next rally scheduled for Faskari Local Government Area on Tuesday, explaining that the decision was deliberate to distinguish the ADC’s approach from that of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). “Today marks the beginning of the change that Katsina people have been yearning for. Everyone you see here came willingly because they desire good governance. I sincerely appreciate our supporters for the warm reception. By the grace of God, we will unveil our agenda in Faskari on Tuesday. We want to show the difference between our campaign and that of the APC-led government,” Kaita declared. Before proceeding to the rally venue, the ADC governorship candidate paid a courtesy visit to the Sarkin Maskan Katsina and District Head of Funtua, where he sought royal blessings, prayers, guidance and support ahead of the elections. The event also featured the ADC senatorial candidate for Funtua zone, Hon. Jamilu Muhammad Lion, whose appearance drew loud cheers from the large gathering of party faithful. The Funtua rally marks the first major campaign outing by Senator Kaita in the 2027 election season and sets the stage for the ADC’s statewide mobilisation as political activities gather momentum across Katsina State. item.title: Bayern’s Musiala suffered another seizure this week
item.description: Bayern Munich and Germany midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered another previously undisclosed seizure this week, according to information received by AFP subsidiary SID on Sunday. The incident, which is categorised by a brief and temporary loss of consciousness or awareness, occurred at training on Monday. Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Monday’s incident was the second since Musiala’s announcement, with the player reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play. News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union FIFPRO for a “coordinated campaign” to pressure the Germany international to renegotiate his 2025-extended contract. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives,” FIFPRO said in a statement. On Friday, Bayern supervisory board member and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the midfielder may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” The post Bayern’s Musiala suffered another seizure this week appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Taraba Yoruba community endorses Tinubu, Kefas for second term
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO – The Yoruba Community Council (YCC) in Taraba State has endorsed President Bola Tinubu and Governor Agbu Kefas for a second term in office, expressing confidence in their leadership and commitment to peace, security and development. The President of the council, Mr Joseph Abiodun Durojaye, announced the endorsement at the 2026 Yoruba Day celebration held over the weekend in Jalingo. The event brought together Yoruba residents from Oyo, Osun, Lagos, Ondo, Kwara, Ogun, Kogi and Ekiti states, among others. Durojaye expressed appreciation to the Kefas administration for its support and goodwill towards the Yoruba community, particularly the appointment of one of its members as a Special Adviser and financial assistance towards the construction of the Yoruba Community Council building. He appealed for continued government support to ensure the completion of the project, saying the building would serve as a permanent centre for community meetings, cultural activities, youth development and other programmes. The community leader formally declared the council’s support for Kefas’s re-election bid, subject to the democratic process and the decision of the electorate. He also expressed support for Tinubu’s re-election for another four-year term. According to him, the community believes in democracy, continuity, peace, security and development, urging both administrations to sustain programmes that improve the lives of Nigerians and promote inclusive governance. Durojaye reaffirmed the Yoruba community’s commitment to peaceful coexistence and cooperation with other ethnic groups in Taraba, describing the state as home to diverse communities. He said the community rejected violence, discrimination, hate speech and other actions capable of undermining unity, insisting that dialogue and mutual understanding remained the best ways to resolve disagreements. In his remarks, Senator Haruna Manu, representing Taraba Central Senatorial District, commended the community for its contributions to the socio-economic development of the state, particularly in commerce, education, agriculture and professional services. Manu, who was represented by Professor Yushau Ahmed Bali, described Taraba as a home for all and urged the Yoruba community to sustain cordial relations with other ethnic groups while promoting peace, unity and peaceful coexistence. He also expressed support for the community’s endorsement of Tinubu and Kefas for another term, urging residents to embrace mutual respect and democratic participation. Similarly, Senator Shuaibu Lau, representing Taraba North Senatorial District, commended the Yoruba community for its political support, describing the endorsement as a demonstration of confidence in the leadership of the President and the governor. item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. ﻿ Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added.
